headline: High risk of prompt-injection and cascading errors if caveman ingests Authelia-authored content via shared files or MCP; compliance and data leakage are lower but non-zero.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Authelia can expose content through OIDC/ForwardAuth and broad network egress, while caveman uses MCP and reads project files like CLAUDE.md. That creates a plausible instruction-bridging path if Authelia-delivered content is later parsed by caveman as trusted text. No direct shared channel is documented, so uncertainty keeps this at medium.
conditions: IF Authelia output is copied into caveman-readable files or MCP messages
IF caveman treats project notes or CLAUDE.md as instructions
mitigations: Restrict Authelia outputs to structured, non-executable fields
Disable automatic ingestion of external text into CLAUDE.md
Add a manual review step before caveman acts on imported content
requires-engineering: add provenance tags to all bridged messages

B_data_leakage.rationale: Authelia is docs-only and touches no listed data classes, while caveman touches session logs, memory files, project notes, and CLAUDE.md. The pair does not show a shared workspace or authenticated principal, so leakage is possible mainly through manual file sharing or copied outputs, with limited blast radius from the documented surfaces.
conditions: IF Authelia-derived content is written into caveman project files
IF caveman session logs or memory files contain copied Authelia outputs
mitigations: Keep Authelia outputs out of shared project directories
Redact secrets before copying text into caveman files
Rotate or isolate any shared credentials
Limit caveman logging for imported content

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Authelia has broad network egress but no filesystem write capability is listed; caveman supports multiple instances and file-based project state, but no write permissions are documented. Because overlapping mutable-resource writes are not evidenced, conflict risk is limited and depends on external orchestration not shown in either profile.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same writable directory
IF an external orchestrator grants both write access to the same mutable resource
mitigations: Separate working directories per agent
Serialize any shared file edits manually
Lock shared files before caveman runs
requires-engineering: add workspace locking in the orchestrator

D_cascading_error.rationale: Caveman is a content-writing agent that can act on project notes and CLAUDE.md, so it may treat upstream text as authoritative. Authelia can emit authentication-related outputs over APIs, which caveman could render or operationalize without verification. The pair lacks a documented verification barrier, making default cascading mistakes plausible.
conditions: IF Authelia-generated text is used as input to caveman writing tasks
IF caveman publishes or edits artifacts without a verification pass
mitigations: Require source attribution on imported text
Add a human verification step before publication
Use a checklist to validate claims from Authelia outputs
requires-engineering: enforce schema validation between agents

E_compliance.rationale: Authelia is an authentication service with broad network egress, while caveman stores session logs, memory files, and project notes. No residency, certification, or retention mismatch is documented, so compliance risk is limited to accidental placement of regulated data into caveman-managed files or logs rather than an inherent pairwise violation.
conditions: IF regulated data is copied into caveman memory files or session logs
IF Authelia outputs include data subject information that is retained in project notes
mitigations: Avoid placing regulated data in caveman files
Set short retention for session logs
Review project notes for sensitive identifiers
requires-engineering: document residency and retention boundaries
